I generally use something like starsan on anything being used for containers or instruments. I'm branching out from beers and ciders to pickles and other fermented foods. It seems daunting, because I don't enjoy losing batches of anything.(i make 5gals at a go brewing) Is this me being paranoid? Following proper procedure?
Am I going overboard sanitizing everything before I do any kind of fermenting?
I generally sanitize everything that is going to come in contact with the wort. Now, there may be something said for allowing natural yeasts to thrive. Let's see what others say.
Wild yeasts are preferred for some hard ciders.

The better I've gotten at sanitizing the more consistent my beer is, so I say fill your boots. The other change I made that was a noticeable benefit is to use filtered water rather than tap water, though I suspect it's more to do with impurities than sanitation. $3 for 5 gallons is not a significant additional cost.

Depends on how perfect/consistent you want the end product to be and how much you want to avoid failure. And also how noticeable 'off' flavours will be in your product.

Going off my own failures, it's probably better to go overboard with sanitation at first while you're learning! :) It's probably a good idea to sanitize well for longer food ferments (kraut goes for 4 weeks) since there's more time for bad bacteria to grow.
